mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals strong consumer demand and construction activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as the equity market prices in improved economic conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where HOUST increases by at least 0.5% over the prior 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 0.4% per annum signals an imminent monetary tightening cycle, which typically causes a contraction in equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises above 0.4%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in payrolls (PAYEMS) and industrial production (INDPRO) above 0.5% over the prior 3 months indicates robust labor market conditions and strong manufacturing output, driving positive equity market returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > 0.5% and INDPRO growth > 0.5% (3-month change)
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where both PAYEMS and INDPRO show growth exceeding 0.5% over the prior 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, rising interest rates (FEDFUNDS) reduce the present value of future cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as investors shift to fixed income.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances during the monetary tightening cycle as defined by FEDFUNDS rising above 0.4%.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) reflects strong manufacturing output and economic activity, which typically correlates with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to improved corporate earnings outlook.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO increases by at least 0.5% over the prior 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4.5% per annum signals a tight labor market, which often precedes wage inflation and corporate margin pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE falls below 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A CPI reading below 240 (year-over-year) indicates low inflation, which supports continued monetary accommodation and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL is below 240.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, rising consumer credit (RSAFS) signals strong household spending and economic momentum, which typically drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the market anticipates continued growth.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances during the late-cycle expansion as defined by RSAFS growth exceeding 1.0%.
